Pennington County Auditor's - Treasurer's Office
The Pennington County Auditor’s Office is part of the administrative branch of County government. The County Auditor is an appointed official responsible for property tax administration, property tax collection, central accounting, license agent, county payroll, elections, passports and is a secretary to the County Board.
Property Tax Payments & Information Online
Property Tax
Calculates proposed and certified tax rates and taxes
Prepares Truth in Taxation notices
Prepares and prints all property tax statements
Maintains ditch and special assessment records
Collects delinquent taxes
Prepares settlement distributions
Completes Tax Searches ($2 / parcel)
Handles Confession of Judgements
Conducts Tax Forfeited Land Sales on behalf of the County
Property Tax Collection The Auditor-Treasurer is the chief financial officer of all county funds and cash assets and handles all funds received or paid out by the County. The Auditor-Treasurer is responsible for investing all county money pursuant to Minnesota Statutes and securing collateral to protect the County funds.
The Auditor-Treasurers office balances and deposits all collections of County funds on a regular basis. Reconciles several bank accounts every month and prepares a trial balance of each fund every month.
The county Auditor-Treasurer's office is responsible for the mailing of approximately 9,500 tax statements annually along with the collection of all real estate, mobile home and personal property taxes. Also maintains escrow accounts on property taxes with escrow agencies.
The due dates of property taxes are: |
First Half Real Estate and Agricultural |
May 15th |
Personal Property |
May 15th |
First Half Mobile Home |
August 31st |
Second Half Real Estate |
October 15th |
Second Half Mobile Home and Agricultural |
November 15th |
A penalty will be applied to all late payments of property taxes in accordance with Minnesota Statutes. The County Auditor-Treasurer is also responsible for the procedures of collection of delinquent Mobile Home taxes.
The Auditor-Treasurer's office processes Deeds for the State Deed Tax before recording with the County Recorders office. These funds are collected along with Mortgage Registration Tax and paid to the State of Minnesota each month.
Each year the County Auditor-Treasurers records and books are audited and must be in compliance with the State Auditors rules and regulations. Reports are prepared and submitted for their audit upon request
Central Accounting
Serves as the central accounting office for the county
Provides financial information for many internal and external requests
Processes the accounts payable for most of the county funds
Processes the accounts receivable for all funds
Coordinates and prepares the annual budget
Prepares schedules for the annual audit
Prepares the financial statement summary for publication
County Capital Assets
Administers insurance records for the county
Maintains county policies
County Payroll
Processes payroll for all county departments
Maintains payroll system database
Administers employee benefits

Election Administration
Serves as the Chief Election Office for the county
Maintains Statewide Voter Registration System data base for Pennington County

Tabulates election results and responsible to report to Secretary of State
Conducts canvassing board

Passports Passport Services
Passport Applications Accepted
8:00 a.m.-4:00 p.m.
Pennington County Auditor/Treasurer's Office
101 Main Avenue North
Thief River Falls, MN 56701
218-683-7000
For the most up-to-date passport and international travel information please visit https://travel.state.gov/content/travel.html , the only official website for:
Downloadable Application Forms
Current Requirements and Fees
Travel Warnings
Consular Information Sheets (on every country in the world)...
Covid Traveling Updates
To obtain a United States Passport you will need to present the following:
A completed passport application (must be signed in person) - this can be obtained from the County Auditor/Treasurer's Office or by clicking on the link above and find the Passport Application.
A certified copy of a Birth Certificate from the County or State level (Not a hospital certificate).
One passport photograph that meets passport requirements (Thrifty White, Walmart and Thoele Photography take passport photographs).
Primary Identification (One of the following):
Previously issued, undamaged U.S. passport
Naturalization Certificate
Valid Driver's License
Current Government ID (city, state or federal)
Current Military ID (military and dependants)
Minors 15 and under must appear with both parents and the parents must present a valid Driver's License. Minors 16 and older, if they have a valid Driver's License, may appear without a parent. If a minor 16 years old or older has no I.D., one parent must appear with the minor.
Fees
Passport Book
Adult: (16 & over)
$130.00 personal check, money order or cashiers check to US Dept of State
$35.00 cash or check to Pennington County Treasurer
Under 16:
$100.00 personal check, money order or cashiers check to US Dept of State
$35.00 cash or check to Pennington County Treasurer
Passport Card
Adult: (16 and over)
$30.00 personal check, money order or cashiers check to US Dept of State
$35.00 cash or check to Pennington County Treasurer
Under 16:
$15.00 personal check, money order or cashiers check to US Dept of State
$35.00 cash or check to Pennington County Treasurer
Combination Adult Passport Book & Card
$160.00 personal check, money order or cashiers check to US Dept of State
$35.00 cash or check to Pennington County Treasurer.
Processing time varies. Please visit https://travel.state.gov/content/travel/en/passports/how-apply/processing-times.html for the most current up to date processing time.
